headline: I2_matcher_accounting is ten rows whose OBSERVATION is a crit. On the one row replayed (19000091/40) the engine's crit arm IS present with damage inside the legal roll window and the renderer simply fails to tag it |-crit|, so the matcher never pairs the two. CONFIRMED ON 1 OF 10. For the other nine the same cause is consistent but NOT established: Case A (the non-crit range straddling the KO) is also untagged, is genuine crit-arm-absence, and presents the same ~2x ratio signature. Distinguishing them needs the branch-mass check recorded below, which has not been run.

the_signature.observation: every one of the ten is a ~2x ratio between the observed direct hit and the engine's majority arm
the_signature.so: a gen3 crit is exactly 2x. These are all critical hits.

but_this_is_NOT_c87.why: C87 was the Sleep Talk path passing branch_on_damage=false, so no crit arm existed. Here the crit arm DOES exist. 19000091/40 offers three arms: 2.34% (leftovers), 93.75% at -26, and 3.91% at -51. The -51 arm is the crit.
but_this_is_NOT_c87.and: all three recursive generate_instructions_from_move call sites now pass branch_on_damage through, so the enumeration is not the gap.

the_actual_cause.worked_example: 19000091/40 -- Medicham's Brick Break crits Ariados for 52 (296 maxhp, |-crit| in the observed protocol). The engine's crit arm carries -51. Magnitude agreement is not the problem: roll_components_agree([-52], [-51], None) returns True in isolation, and 52 sits inside the window 45.9-56.6.
the_actual_cause.what_rejects_it: the crit cross-check at engine_transition_differential.py:1342. `observed_component.critical is not support.critical` returns False outright, regardless of magnitude.
the_actual_cause.why_support_critical_is_wrong: support.critical comes from _direct_hit_is_critical(events, ...), which reads the ENGINE BRANCH'S RENDERED PROTOCOL for a |-crit| line. It does not read the engine's own crit flag.
the_actual_cause.the_renderer_gate: rust/pokezero-search/src/events.rs:2156-2162 emits |-crit| only when Some(damage.damage_amount) == crit_collapsed EXACTLY, and crit_collapsed != regular_collapsed, and the hit is not a KO. An EXACT-VALUE equality. A crit arm produced by the KO-STRADDLE path (Case B with a straddle) carries a damage value that is not byte-equal to the single collapsed crit value, so it goes untagged. A NON-straddling crit arm is set to exactly that value and IS tagged correctly -- see MECHANISM_IS_STRADDLE_CONDITIONAL.
the_actual_cause.the_chain: renderer omits |-crit| -> _direct_hit_is_critical returns False -> support.critical False -> the cross-check rejects an observed crit against the engine's own crit arm, on identity rather than on magnitude.

disposition.class: MATCHER or RENDERER FIX, not an engine gap
disposition.why_not_engine: the crit arm is present in the support with a magnitude that agrees. Nothing is missing from the engine.
disposition.the_fix: there is no crit flag at the render site -- instruction.rs:515-518 is DamageInstruction { side_ref, damage_amount } and nothing more. C77 recorded the implementable form: carry the BRANCH'S OWN roll representative into crit_collapsed so the two are comparable by construction. For the crit-KILL arm that is not sufficient on its own, because the KO guard blocks it independently; Showdown does emit |-crit| on a killing crit, so that guard needs revisiting too.
disposition.prediction_if_fixed: deliberately not registered as a numeric prediction. The row count this closes should be measured by single-variable re-sweep, not forecast.

honest_gap_in_this_finding: NARROWED, not closed. The gap was 'I have not directly observed the absence of the |-crit| line in these ten branches'. scripts/replay_residue.py CANNOT observe that: it feeds branch['events'] straight into damage_components (:121-127) and prints only per-slot component tuples (:129-136); the only protocol lines it prints are the OBSERVED Showdown slice (:72-76). The engine branch's rendered lines are never displayed. What replay closed is a DIFFERENT gap -- fragment versus complete branch set. Tag absence is still inferred here, though C77 measured it directly at the gate on 451 evaluations.

REPLAY_CONFIRMATION.method: scripts/replay_residue.py, which re-derives each branch's FULL component set against the vendored engine. This is the method c94 establishes as correct; branch_misses cannot answer it, because it reports one slot per branch.

engine_branches.93.75%: p1 itemleftovers=+14 | p2 itemleftovers=+18, move=-26   (non-crit arm)
engine_branches.3.91%: p1 itemleftovers=+14 | p2 itemleftovers=+18, move=-51   (THE CRIT ARM)

REPLAY_CONFIRMATION.what_it_establishes: the 3.91% arm matches the observation on EVERY component -- both Leftovers ticks exact -- and differs only on the direct hit, -51 against -52, which passes in isolation (window around 51 is 45.9 to 56.6). The crit arm is present, complete and numerically agreeing, and the row is still divergent.
REPLAY_CONFIRMATION.therefore: by elimination over a COMPLETE branch set rather than a fragment, the only remaining rejector is the crit cross-check at engine_transition_differential.py:1342, which fails when observed.critical is not support.critical. The observation carries |-crit|, so support.critical is False -- the renderer did not tag the engine's own crit arm. That is the exact-value gate at events.rs:2156-2162.
REPLAY_CONFIRMATION.c94s_trap_in_miniature: the 2.34% arm's miss string reads 'obs=[itemleftovers 14] eng=[]', which my retracted method would have read as an arm at net 0. Replay shows p2 capped_lethal=-55 with no p1 components -- the miss reported p1's complaint only. The fragment happened to be accurate FOR p1, which is exactly why the error stayed invisible.

NAMING_CORRECTION: an earlier version of this file was headed 'crit-arm-absence', which is the C77/C87 shape name and the OPPOSITE of this finding. A reader indexing on the headline would have got the retracted claim.

the_mechanism_why_the_values_differ.this_is_the_load_bearing_step: an earlier version asserted the values differ without saying why, which would let a reader assume both are the engine's collapsed crit damage and conclude the gate fires fine.
the_mechanism_why_the_values_differ.crit_collapsed: events.rs:2494-2533 expected_damage_values sets crit_collapsed = (max_crit_damage as f32 * 0.925) as i16.
the_mechanism_why_the_values_differ.what_the_arm_actually_carries: third_party/poke-engine-gen3-crit-kill-split.patch partitions the crit arm into crit-kill (damage = defender_active.hp) and crit-survive (damage = average_non_kill_crit_damage). in general NEITHER equals (max_crit_damage * 0.925) as i16 -- and for the crit-KILL arm the operative blocker is the KO guard rather than value inequality.
the_mechanism_why_the_values_differ.worked: 19000091/40: max_noncrit 29 -> regular_collapsed int(26.825) = 26 (matches the -26 arm); max_crit 58 -> crit_collapsed int(53.65) = 53; crit-survive average over the 10 non-lethal rolls = 51.4 -> 51 (matches the crit arm). 51 != 53, so the gate does not fire. Masses check exactly: 93.75% = 1-1/16, 3.91% = (1/16)(10/16), 2.34% = (1/16)(6/16).

already_measured_by_C77.note: C77 established this same root cause by INSTRUMENTATION, which is stronger than this report's re-derivation. It should have been cited from the start.
already_measured_by_C77.evidence: reports/c77_i2_crit_arm_absence.json condition_identified_by_instrumentation -- 451 evaluations instrumented at the gate, 'exact value match against crit_collapsed: 449 (99.6%)', and the_answer: 'the blocker is Some(damage.damage_amount) == crit_collapsed, an EXACT equality.'
already_measured_by_C77.consequence: this report's novelty is narrower than an earlier draft implied. Its contribution is tying the ten CURRENT-ERA rows to that already-measured blocker and naming the crit-kill-split as the reason the values differ.

evidence_strength: confirmed on 1 row by replay (19000091/40), inferred on 9. The ratio table establishes per-row that the OBSERVATION is a crit -- all ten ratios are achievable as (legal crit roll)/(collapsed non-crit arm), including the apparent outlier 62/28. It does NOT establish per-row that the crit ARM is present, which is this report's actual claim and precisely the axis C77 measured as splitting ~217 engine-gap / 173 renderer-gap.
unremarked_precondition: the :1342 cross-check only fires when support is not None, which needs a pre-damage |switch| or nonzero boost in the ENGINE branch's events (_event_changes_roll_state :612-626, gated :697-716). The conclusion survives -- legal is accept-only and never a veto (:953-957), so with support None the branch would have MATCHED and the row would not be divergent, hence support must be non-None -- but 'the only remaining rejector' depends on a structural condition this report did not check.
not_the_largest_family: LS_capped_lethal_shape is 12 rows in reports/c86 and also unadjudicated. I2 at 10 is the second largest.

MECHANISM_IS_STRADDLE_CONDITIONAL.correction: an earlier revision of the mechanism text overreached, saying ANY crit arm not byte-equal to crit_collapsed goes untagged. Those sentences are now EDITED IN PLACE above rather than corrected from here, so the document reads correctly top-to-bottom. There are four paths that set a crit arm's damage and this mechanism covers one.

the_four_paths.path: Case A -- the NON-CRIT range straddles the KO (generate_instructions.rs:3006-3032)
the_four_paths.arm: crit mass is MERGED INTO THE KO ARM at defender_active.hp; branch_chance at :3025 is (1-crit_rate)(k/16) + crit_rate
the_four_paths.tagged: no -- and NO DISTINCT CRIT ARM EXISTS. This is genuine crit-arm-absence, the C77 217-row bucket and the OPPOSITE of this report's finding. Documented at docs/crate_search_design.md:264-265.

the_four_paths.path: Case B -- the CRIT range straddles the KO (:3051-3076)
the_four_paths.arm: crit-kill at defender_active.hp (:3069), crit-survive at average_non_kill_crit_damage (:3074)
the_four_paths.tagged: no -- THIS is this report's mechanism
YES, byte-identical to crit_collapsed. The gate fires correctly. This is the COMMON case.

MECHANISM_IS_STRADDLE_CONDITIONAL.consequence_for_the_headline: the mechanism implies a testable precondition: each of the ten rows must be Case B-with-straddle. A non-straddling crit gets tagged and cannot be in this family at all. But it does NOT license 'all ten, one cause', because CASE A IS ALSO UNTAGGED and is genuine crit-arm-absence -- a Case A row presents the same ~2x ratio signature and would be misfiled here.
MECHANISM_IS_STRADDLE_CONDITIONAL.how_to_settle_it_cheaply: the branch-mass fingerprint separates them with no instrumentation and no rebuild. Case A: two arms, the KO arm's mass INCLUDING the crit rate. Case B-straddle: three arms whose two small arms sum to exactly crit_rate (the 93.75 / 3.91 / 2.34 already collected on 19000091/40). Case B-no-straddle: 93.75 / 6.25, and tagged. One replay_residue.py run per row, reading only percentages.
MECHANISM_IS_STRADDLE_CONDITIONAL.status: NOT RUN for the nine unreplayed rows. Case A is an unexcluded alternative for them.

precision_on_NEITHER_equals: for the crit-KILL arm the operative blocker is the KO guard (damage.damage_amount < pre_hp fails when damage == defender_active.hp), not value inequality -- and defender_active.hp COULD coincidentally equal int(max_crit * 0.925). For the crit-SURVIVE arm, average_non_kill_crit_damage can in principle land on that value when the kill threshold sits near the top of the roll fan. 'In general does not equal' is the correct claim; C77's 449 of 451 rather than 451/451 is consistent with exactly this.
C77_measured_the_condition_but_its_EXPLA: C77's the_answer attributes the mismatch to the engine collapsing its roll fan to at most three representatives (DamageRolls Average|Min|Max) with the rendered branch not carrying the same representative. In gen3 that is not what happens: calculate_damage_rolls requests DamageRolls::Max (gen3/generate_instructions.rs:5124) and the renderer applies the single 0.925 itself, so crit_collapsed IS the Average representative by construction. C77 measured WHICH condition fires correctly; its account of WHY is wrong, and the crit-kill-split is the real answer. This report supersedes C77's explanation while deferring to its measurement.
C77_449_of_451_is_conditioned: C77's method line says it replayed the I2 crit rows -- rows selected BECAUSE the match failed. Given that Case B-no-straddle tags correctly, 99.6% cannot be a general property of the gate. It is a rate within an already-failing population, not a base rate.
EDITING_DISCIPLINE: review round three found this file had accumulated five correction keys sitting BELOW the claims they corrected, so a reader going top-to-bottom -- or grepping a field name -- hit the retracted version while the correction sat 40 lines further down under a key they had no reason to look for. That is structurally the same failure as C94: the artifact looks authoritative and the error stays invisible. Corrections are now applied IN PLACE; this key is the changelog.
line_citation_durability: engine citations point into third_party/poke-engine-src, which is NOT tracked in git (fetched by scripts/vendor_poke_engine_src.sh), so those line numbers can drift with no diff and are not reproducible from the repo alone. third_party/poke-engine-gen3-crit-kill-split.patch IS tracked and is the durable citation for the mechanism.
